alate: The dealate adult has the head deep brownish yellow, compound eyes blackish brown, ocelli, antennae, labrum and postmentum pale yellowish brown, pronotum slightly paler than the head capsule, legs and abdomen pale yellowish brown. Head nearly circular, compound eyes oblong, their short diameter more than twice the distance from the eye to the lower margin of the head capsule; ocelli oval, close to the compound eyes; antennal spots and epicranial suture indistinct; antennae with ten segments, the second to fourth nearly equal in length. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head capsule or as wide as the head capsule (including the compound eyes).
soldier: The soldier has the head capsule yellowish brown tinged with red, mandibles purplish brown, labrum, antennae and pronotum pale brown, abdomen and legs pale yellowish brown. Head capsule elongate-cylindrical, the sides parallel, the posterior margin straight; in profile the dorsolateral frontal angle raised, the frontal slope about 60 degrees, the anterolateral frontal angles also projecting, the dorsal margin of the head and the ventral margin of the postmentum both nearly straight, the frontal surface a shallow V-shaped depression between the two dorsolateral frontal angles; neither the Y-shaped suture nor the ocelli visible, the compound eyes discernible. Labrum nearly circular, mandibles short and stout with rather curved tips, the basal prominence of the mandible distinct, the left mandible shorter than half the head capsule. Antennae with 13 segments. The postmentum seven to eight times as long as the waist, the broadest region before the anterior third, several transverse striae behind the anterior margin, the lateral lobes distinct, the waist region in the posterior third. The pronotum narrower than the head capsule, the anterior margin with a broad shallow V-shaped concavity, the lateral margins oblique backwards, the middle of the posterior margin very shallowly concave.
